title: Kotlin Fundamentals
content: Kotlin is a modern, statically typed language. Key features include null safety, extension functions, and higher-order functions which make Android development more concise and robust.

title: Jetpack Compose Basics
content: Compose is Android's modern toolkit for building native UI. It simplifies UI development with a declarative approach, allowing you to describe your UI and let Compose handle the rendering.

title: Clean Architecture
content: Separating concerns into Data, Domain, and Presentation layers. This makes your code more testable, maintainable, and independent of external frameworks or databases.

title: Hilt Dependency Injection
content: Hilt provides a standard way to use Dagger DI in your Android app. It simplifies the setup and manages the lifecycle of dependencies automatically.

title: Coroutines & Flow
content: Managing background tasks efficiently without blocking the main thread. Flow provides a reactive stream of data that can be observed in the UI.

title: Retrofit Networking
content: The most popular HTTP client for Android. It turns your API into a Java interface using annotations, making network calls type-safe and easy.

title: Room Database
content: The recommended way to persist data locally. It provides an abstraction layer over SQLite and allows compile-time verification of queries.

title: ViewModel & State
content: Storing and managing UI-related data in a lifecycle-conscious way. ViewModels survive configuration changes like screen rotations.

title: Navigation Component
content: Simplifying navigation between screens. It handles the back stack and argument passing in a consistent way.

title: WorkManager
content: For tasks that need to run even if the app exits or the device reboots. Perfect for syncing data or uploading logs.

title: Swift Fundamentals
content: Swift is a powerful and intuitive programming language for iOS, macOS, tvOS, and watchOS. It's safe, fast, and interactive, with features like optionals and type inference.

title: SwiftUI Essentials
content: SwiftUI helps you build great-looking apps across all Apple platforms with the power of Swift. Build user interfaces for any Apple device using just one set of tools and APIs.

title: ARC & Memory Management
content: Automatic Reference Counting (ARC) handles memory management for you in Swift. Understanding strong, weak, and unowned references is key to avoiding retain cycles.

title: RESTful API Design
content: REST (Representational State Transfer) is an architectural style for providing standards between computer systems on the web, making it easier for systems to communicate with each other.

title: Microservices Architecture
content: Microservices are an architectural and organizational approach to software development where software is composed of small independent services that communicate over well-defined APIs.

title: SQL vs NoSQL
content: Relational databases (SQL) use structured schemas and are great for complex queries. NoSQL databases are more flexible and scale horizontally, ideal for large volumes of unstructured data.

title: React Hooks
content: Hooks allow you to use state and other React features without writing a class. They let you split one component into smaller functions based on what pieces are related.

title: CSS Flexbox
content: Flexbox is a one-dimensional layout method for arranging items in rows or columns. Items flex to fill additional space and shrink to fit into smaller spaces.

title: Typography Hierarchy
content: Using different font sizes and weights to guide the user's attention. Good hierarchy makes content easy to scan and understand.

title: Color Theory
content: Understanding how colors interact and influence emotions. Choosing the right color palette is crucial for establishing brand identity and mood.

title: Python for Data Science
content: Python is the most popular language for data science due to its simplicity and powerful libraries like Pandas, NumPy, and Scikit-learn.

title: Machine Learning Basics
content: Machine learning is a type of artificial intelligence (AI) that allows software applications to become more accurate at predicting outcomes without being explicitly programmed.
